name: Braintrust
tagline: Hosted platform for evaluating, logging and iterating on LLM applications: datasets, scorers, trace viewing and a prompt playground.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core loop here is not magic: run a task function over a dataset of inputs, score the outputs with a handful of graders, store the results, and diff run A against run B. An agent can build that locally in a sitting, and the scoring library pattern (LLM-as-judge plus deterministic string and JSON checks) is well trodden public knowledge. Where it gets thin is everything around the loop: ingesting production traces at volume, a review UI other people will actually use, a playground that speaks to every provider, and the CI integration that makes evals a gate instead of a hobby. For one developer babysitting one or two prompts, a local runner plus a results table is honestly enough. For a team where three people argue about whether the new prompt regressed, the hosted thing starts earning its keep.
coreLoopDIY: Runs your task function over a versioned dataset, scores each output with deterministic and LLM-judge graders, writes every run to SQLite, and serves a web view to compare two runs row by row.
requirements: An API key for at least one model provider, in .env
Your app logic importable as a plain function
Willingness to write your own scorers for anything domain specific
whatYouLose: Production trace ingestion and search at real volume, with sampling and retention
A shared review queue where non-engineers label outputs and those labels flow back into datasets
The multi-provider playground and prompt versioning that lives outside your repo
Maintained autoeval scorers and the tuning that went into them
Team permissions, audit trails and the ability to point at a URL in a pull request
moatNotes: The defensible part is the human workflow around evals, not the eval math. Once three people and a CI pipeline depend on the same run history, leaving gets expensive.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because evals are the chore nobody wants to own. A local runner works great until someone asks for the trace from last Tuesday, a PM wants to grade fifty outputs without cloning your repo, and CI needs a stable artifact to compare against. Paying converts an internal tool that one engineer maintains into infrastructure the whole team can point at, which is usually cheaper than that engineer's attention.
notes: The eval loop is a weekend; the review workflow is the product. Build the local runner first and see whether you actually miss the rest.
prompt:
Build a local LLM evaluation harness. Stack: Python 3.12, uv for deps, SQLite via sqlite3 (no ORM), FastAPI with Jinja2 templates for the UI. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry. Model keys come from .env via python-dotenv.

CLI, exposed as `evals`:
- `evals dataset add NAME path/to/file.jsonl` : imports rows of {input, expected?, metadata?}, stores a content hash so dataset versions are distinguishable.
- `evals run --dataset NAME --task module:function --scorers exact,json_match,llm_judge --tag "prompt-v3"` : imports the task callable, runs it over every row with a bounded thread pool and retries, records per-row output, latency, token counts if the provider returns them, and each scorer's numeric score plus rationale.
- `evals compare RUN_A RUN_B` : prints a per-scorer mean delta and the ten rows that moved the most.
- `evals serve` : starts the web UI on localhost:8000.

Scorers live in scorers.py as plain functions taking (input, output, expected) and returning (score float 0..1, rationale str). Ship four: exact_match, includes, json_match (deep compare with key order ignored), and llm_judge (a single chat call to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, base URL and model from .env, returns a 0..1 score and one sentence of reasoning, parsed from strict JSON with one retry on parse failure).

Schema: datasets, dataset_rows, runs, results, scores. Every run stores the task reference, scorer list, dataset hash, git commit if available, and a free-text tag.

Web UI, server-rendered, no build step, minimal CSS:
- Run list with dataset, tag, timestamp and mean score per scorer.
- Run detail: table of rows with input, output, expected, per-scorer scores, expandable rationale, sortable by score ascending so failures surface first.
- Compare view for two run ids, side by side outputs with score deltas highlighted.
- A button on any row to write it back into a dataset as a regression case.

Explicitly out of scope: authentication, multi-user review queues, production trace ingestion, streaming, a prompt playground, hosted deployment.

Include a seed dataset of 20 rows, one example task in example_task.py, a pytest suite covering the scorers and the compare math, and a README with the exact commands to go from empty folder to a comparison view in under five minutes.
